blocks.text: Surrey Court-Ordered Sales: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Surrey's tax sale is a separate City process, not a foreclosure: the City states it is required by the Local Government Act to sell at tax sale all properties whose taxes have not been paid for three years.

The City sells at the Upset Price: the tax sale page states the Collector may sell a property for the Upset Price, which equals all outstanding taxes, penalties, interest, 5% tax sale costs, and Land Title Office fees.
The City gives no warranty on a tax sale property: the tax sale page states all property sales are "as is" without warranty or guarantee by the City.

blocks.text: Surrey Court-Ordered Sales: costs and taxes

items.t: Surrey's 2026 municipal tax rate for residential (Class 1) property totals 1.84251 per $1,000 of assessed value on the City's 2026 rate schedule.
Surrey's 2026 annual flat water and sewer rates for a single-family dwelling total $2,856: water $1,195 and sewer $1,661.
Surrey's 2026 waste collection charge for a single-family dwelling is $344.08 for garbage, recycling and organics, collected with property taxes and due July 2 each year.
The tax sale happens at Surrey City Hall: the City's 2025 notice places the auction in the Council Chambers at Surrey City Hall, 13450 104 Avenue, Surrey.

blocks.text: Surrey Court-Ordered Sales: risks and due diligence

items.t: A lowland Surrey property can sit in the coastal floodplain: the City states its coastal floodplain covers about 20% of Surrey's land area, stretching from Boundary Bay and Mud Bay along the Nicomekl and Serpentine Rivers toward Cloverdale and Newton, and is subject to coastal and river flooding.

Most of that floodplain sits behind dykes, not above the water: the City states most of Surrey's floodplain, coastal and inland, is protected by dykes, with sea dams on the Nicomekl and Serpentine Rivers first built in 1912 and 1913.
A tax sale title carries the redemption risk for a year: the City states the owner may redeem within one year of the tax sale by paying all taxes, interest, and charges.

faq.q: When is Surrey's tax sale, and how do I bid?
faq.a: Surrey holds its annual tax sale at 10:00 a.m. on the last Monday of September in Council Chambers at Surrey City Hall, 13450 104 Avenue. Bidders register at the Property & Payment Services counter at City Hall starting 8:30 a.m. that day, and registration closes at 9:59 a.m., with late registration not permitted.

faq.q: If I buy at the Surrey tax sale, is the property mine right away?
faq.a: No, the sale sits under a one-year redemption right. The City states the current owner has one year after the property is sold at tax sale to pay all taxes, interest, and charges to retain ownership of the property, so a tax sale purchaser waits out that year before the purchase is secure.

faq.q: How do I keep a Surrey property out of the tax sale list?
faq.a: Pay the delinquent taxes before the deadlines the City publishes. The City states properties that may be included in the tax sale are listed in the local newspaper the week before the sale, that paying delinquent taxes by September 2 avoids the newspaper listing, and that paying before 10:00 a.m. on tax sale day removes the property from the list.

faq.q: What is a court-ordered sale in Surrey Foreclosures and Court Sales?
faq.a: It is a sale of a property supervised by the court after a lender has taken legal action, and the sale needs court approval. Offers are usually made subject to that approval, and other buyers can sometimes bid higher at the hearing.

faq.q: Can I put conditions on an offer for a foreclosure in Surrey Foreclosures and Court Sales?
faq.a: Conditions such as financing or inspection may be limited or not accepted, depending on the lender's and the court's terms. Speak to Jared and your lawyer before you write an offer.
